title: Linux Command Line Basics
description: Sample bank covering common Linux shell commands and concepts (demo data).

questions.q: Which command prints the current working directory?
questions.explain: pwd stands for 'print working directory' and outputs the absolute path of where you currently are in the filesystem.

questions.q: What does the command 'cd ..' do?
questions.explain: '..' refers to the parent directory, so 'cd ..' moves the shell up one level in the directory tree.

questions.q: Which flag makes 'ls' show hidden files?
questions.explain: 'ls -a' lists all entries including hidden files and directories, which start with a dot.

questions.q: Which command copies files?
questions.explain: cp copies files or directories; mv moves or renames them, and rm deletes them.

questions.q: What does 'rm -rf' do when run on a directory?
questions.correct: Recursively and forcibly deletes it without confirmation
distractors: Renames it to a backup file
Moves it to a trash folder
questions.explain: -r makes rm recurse into directories, and -f suppresses confirmation prompts, so 'rm -rf' deletes a directory tree immediately and irreversibly.

questions.q: Which command creates a new empty directory?
questions.explain: mkdir creates a new directory; touch creates or updates the timestamp of a file, not a directory.

questions.q: What does 'touch file.txt' do if file.txt doesn't exist?
questions.correct: Creates an empty file named file.txt
distractors: Prints an error since the file is missing
questions.explain: touch creates the file if it doesn't already exist, or updates its modification timestamp if it does.

questions.q: What does the permission string 'rwxr-xr--' mean for the file owner?
questions.explain: The first three characters represent the owner's permissions: r (read), w (write), x (execute) — all three are present here.

questions.q: Which command changes file ownership?
questions.explain: chown changes the owner (and optionally group) of a file. chmod changes permissions, and chgrp changes only the group.

questions.q: What does 'chmod 755 script.sh' set the permissions to?
questions.correct: Owner: read/write/execute, group and others: read/execute
distractors: Owner: read only, everyone else: no access
questions.explain: 755 in octal breaks down to rwx (7) for owner, r-x (5) for group, and r-x (5) for others.

questions.q: Which command lists currently running processes?
questions.explain: ps displays information about active processes. 'top' shows a live, continuously updating view rather than a single snapshot list.

questions.q: Which signal does 'kill -9' send to a process?
questions.explain: Signal 9 is SIGKILL, which forcibly terminates a process immediately without allowing cleanup. SIGTERM (15) is the default, gentler signal.

questions.q: What does appending '&' to a command do?
questions.correct: Runs the command in the background
distractors: Pipes the output to another command
Runs the command with elevated privileges
questions.explain: Appending & runs the job in the background, returning control of the shell immediately.

questions.q: Which command searches for a text pattern within files?
questions.explain: grep searches file contents for lines matching a pattern. 'find' searches for files by name or attribute, not content.

questions.q: What does the pipe symbol '|' do in a shell command?
questions.correct: Sends the output of one command as input to another
distractors: Runs two commands simultaneously in parallel
Comments out the rest of the line
questions.explain: The pipe connects the standard output of the command on its left to the standard input of the command on its right.

questions.q: Which command displays the last few lines of a file by default?
questions.explain: tail shows the end of a file (last 10 lines by default). head shows the beginning instead.

questions.q: On a Debian-based system, which command is used to install a package?
questions.explain: Debian and Ubuntu use APT as their package manager, so 'apt install' (or the older 'apt-get install') installs packages.

questions.q: Which command shows disk space usage for filesystems?
questions.explain: df reports filesystem-level disk usage, while du reports usage for specific files and directories.

questions.q: What does the 'sudo' command do?
questions.correct: Runs a command with superuser (root) privileges
distractors: Switches to another user's home directory
Schedules a command to run later
questions.explain: sudo (superuser do) temporarily elevates a permitted user's privileges to execute a command as root.

questions.q: What does '>' do when used after a command?
questions.correct: Redirects standard output to a file, overwriting it
distractors: Redirects standard input from a file
questions.explain: A single '>' redirects stdout to the named file, creating it if needed and overwriting any existing content. '>>' appends instead.

questions.q: Which file descriptor number represents standard error (stderr)?
questions.explain: By convention, 0 is stdin, 1 is stdout, and 2 is stderr.
